This indicates continued community interest and benchmarking activity around Meta's latest large language models.

stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on the Hugging Face platform.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its primary function as a large language model (LLM).
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, placing it within the current LLM ecosystem.

stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function.
It is associated with key AI/ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-V4-Pro model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation and conversational AI pipelines.
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a substantial community of 8.9 million developers.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 when running on Apple Silicon.
The speed improvement is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) leveraging the MLX framework.
Performance gains reach up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in its MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It targets complex, long-running agent workflows in AI applications.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents entirely on local, personal hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM integration.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, enhancing local AI capabilities on Macs.
The feature is currently available in a preview state, indicating ongoing development and adoption.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It connects these apps to local AI coding agents.
A key feature is that all AI processing runs entirely on the user's local device, emphasizing privacy.

stories.title: Quantum error correction can constantly recalibrate a processor
stories.author: John Timmer
bullet_points: Quantum error correction is being advanced through continuous recalibration of processors.
Reinforcement learning is employed as the mechanism to drive this correction.
The system uses real-time error information to dynamically adjust control algorithms.

stories.title: Ransomware negotiator hired to represent victims was working for the attackers
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A ransomware negotiator was found to be working for the attackers, betraying his clients.
The individual was sentenced to six years in prison for his actions.
The story highlights the severe risks and ethical breaches within the cybersecurity incident response industry.

stories.title: AUTOPILOT VQA: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Incident-Centric Dashcam Understanding
stories.author: Jugal Kalita
bullet_points: Introduces AUTOPILOT-VQA, a new benchmark specifically designed for incident-centric visual question answering in dashcam video.
Addresses a critical gap in current Vision-Language Model (VLM) evaluation: assessing reliable reasoning about safety-critical driving incidents.
Leverages recent advancements in VLMs and LLMs to push the boundaries of autonomous driving understanding.

stories.title: The Illusion of Equivalency: Statistical Characterization of Quantization Effects in LLMs
stories.author: Carson K. Leung
bullet_points: Current LLM quantization evaluation (accuracy/perplexity) is insufficient because it misses behavioral changes.
The paper introduces 'correctness agreement,' a new decision-level metric to assess quantization impact.
This metric measures the overlap in correct predictions between a base and quantized LLM, independent of absolute accuracy.

stories.title: Super Weights in LLMs and the Failure of Selective Training
stories.author: Akarsha Sehwag
bullet_points: Identifies 'Super Weights' in LLMs—individual parameters whose removal drastically reduces model performance.
Challenges the assumption that Super Weight-aware training is effective, showing that training these critical parameters in isolation degrades accuracy.
Demonstrates that the impact of Super Weights is not universal across all Large Language Models (LLMs).

stories.title: UniClawBench: A Universal Benchmark for Proactive Agents on Real-World Tasks
stories.author: Xihui Liu
bullet_points: Introduces UniClawBench, a new universal benchmark designed to evaluate proactive AI agents.
Addresses limitations in current benchmarks, which often use sandboxed environments and single-turn evaluations.
Aims to provide a more robust evaluation framework for real-world, complex tasks performed by LLMs and multimodal agents.

stories.title: WebSwarm: Recursive Multi-Agent Orchestration for Deep-and-Wide Web Search
stories.author: Zhicheng Dou
bullet_points: WebSwarm introduces a recursive multi-agent orchestration framework to overcome limitations in current LLM-based web search.
It addresses the constraint of single ReAct agents being limited by trajectory length and context window when handling complex, deep-and-wide research tasks.
The system aims to improve upon existing multi-agent methods by specifically enhancing recursive search depth and coverage.

stories.title: UltraX: Refining Pre-Training Data at Scale with Adaptive Programmatic Editing
stories.author: Zhiyuan Liu
bullet_points: Addresses the diminishing returns of scaling laws as training data nears physical limits for LLMs.
Proposes 'UltraX,' a method for refining pre-training data at scale using adaptive programmatic editing.
Aims to overcome limitations of existing refinement methods, such as the inflexibility of rule-based approaches.

stories.title: It Takes a MAESTRO To Prune Bad Experts
stories.author: Tanmoy Chakraborty
bullet_points: Addresses a critical deployment bottleneck in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models: the need to keep large expert banks in memory.
Introduces MAESTRO, a new method designed to prune 'bad experts' in MoE models.
Overcomes limitations of existing pruning techniques by accounting for the interdependent nature of MoE routing, unlike methods designed for dense transformers.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces significant performance improvements.
Enhanced GGUF model compatibility is now supported via llama.cpp integration.
The update broadens model support across various hardware, augmenting the MLX engine on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The update also introduces web search capabilities to Claude Code via Ollama.
This suggests an enhancement in the complexity and real-time capability of AI coding assistants.

stories.title: Apple’s failed self-driving car program left a legacy of powerful AI chips
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Apple's stalled self-driving car project was a catalyst for developing powerful on-device AI processing capabilities.
The necessity of high-performance AI processing for the autonomous driving platform drove chip innovation at Apple.
The story suggests that the ambition of the failed car program contributed significantly to the current strength of Apple's AI chips.

stories.title: China recovered its first reusable rocket and showed a new way to do it
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: China has successfully recovered its first reusable rocket.
The recovery demonstrated a new method for achieving reusability.
The effort is viewed as an attempt by China to replicate technologies pioneered by SpaceX.

stories.title: OpenCoF: Learning to Reason Through Video Generation
stories.author: Hongsheng Li
bullet_points: Introduces OpenCoF, a new approach to enabling reasoning within video generation models.
Proposes Chain-of-Frame (CoF) reasoning as a temporal alternative to traditional Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning.
Addresses the current limitation of video generators lacking specific supervision for complex CoF reasoning.

stories.title: Ideas Have Genomes: Benchmarking Scientific Lineage Reasoning and Lineage-Grounded Idea Generation
stories.author: Xue Yang
bullet_points: Introduces IdeaGene-Bench (IG-Bench), a new benchmark designed to test AI's ability to reason about the lineage of scientific ideas.
Addresses the gap in current AI evaluation by modeling scientific ideas as having an 'inheritance structure,' similar to biological genomes.
Focuses on benchmarking both scientific lineage reasoning and the generation of new ideas grounded in existing work.

stories.title: Using AI-based Learning Assistants in Higher Education: A Large-Scale Descriptive Analysis
stories.author: Valerie Heckel
bullet_points: The study provides a large-scale, objective analysis of AI learning assistant usage (Syntea) in higher education.
It analyzes usage patterns across diverse student demographics, including gender, age, and degree.
The research addresses a gap in current literature by moving beyond small samples and self-reported data to examine actual usage behavior.

stories.title: Dimensionality Reduction Meets Network Science: Sensemaking on UMAP's kNN Graph
stories.author: Dominik Moritz
bullet_points: The research focuses on leveraging the internal k-nearest-neighbor (kNN) graph constructed by UMAP, rather than just its final low-dimensional embedding.
This internal graph preserves the data manifold structure in the original high-dimensional space, avoiding projection distortion.
Applying standard graph algorithms to this latent graph enhances data sensemaking capabilities.

stories.title: Workflow as Knowledge: Semantic Persistence for LLM-Mediated Workflows
stories.author: Francesco Zanitti
bullet_points: Proposes a language-independent conceptual model for managing LLM-mediated workflows.
Focuses on 'Semantic Persistence' to handle workflow definitions, instances, and inference records.
Utilizes Lisp-inspired concepts like symbolic forms and object identity as explanatory frameworks.

stories.title: Validity of LLMs as data annotators: AMALIA on authority
stories.author: Manuel Pita
bullet_points: A publicly funded, 9B-parameter LLM (AMALIA) for European Portuguese is being tested as a data annotator.
AMALIA shows competitive agreement with human coders on tasks like defining the moral foundation of authority.
The paper cautions that high agreement only indicates reliability, not necessarily validity, for complex theoretical constructs.

stories.title: Pose-to-Biomechanics: Bridging 3D Human Pose Estimation and Biomechanical Attribute Prediction
stories.author: Kevin Desai
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap where 3D human pose estimation focuses on geometric accuracy, while real-world applications need biomechanical insights.
A new lightweight temporal transformer, 'BioModule,' is proposed to bridge the gap between pose estimation and biomechanical attribute prediction.
The technology has relevance across fields such as rehabilitation, sports science, ergonomics, and clinical movement analysis.

stories.title: Score Accuracy Along the Forward Diffusion Does Not Certify Numerical Stability in Diffusion Sampling
stories.author: Yiwei Zhou
bullet_points: The paper challenges the assumption that low forward-marginal error in diffusion models guarantees numerical stability during sampling.
It demonstrates that a smooth score field with minimal forward error can still lead to a nonexplosive, stable reverse-time process.
This highlights a critical distinction between theoretical error bounds (forward marginals) and practical stability during discrete sampling.

stories.title: Dimensionality Reduction Meets Network Science: Sensemaking on UMAP's kNN Graph
stories.author: Dominik Moritz
bullet_points: The paper explores the underutilized k-nearest-neighbor (kNN) graph constructed internally by UMAP.
This internal graph preserves the data manifold structure in the original high-dimensional space, unlike the final low-dimensional projection.
Applying standard graph algorithms to this internal graph can enhance data sensemaking beyond typical UMAP usage.

stories.title: ARDY: Autoregressive Diffusion with Hybrid Representation for Interactive Human Motion Generation
stories.author: Davis Rempe
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical need for real-time, interactive 3D human motion generation.
It proposes ARDY, an Autoregressive Diffusion model utilizing a Hybrid Representation to bridge the gap between offline control and online speed.
The work aims to overcome limitations in existing methods, specifically the lack of inference speed in controlled offline models and poor controllability in fast online methods.

stories.title: Pose-to-Biomechanics: Bridging 3D Human Pose Estimation and Biomechanical Attribute Prediction
stories.author: Kevin Desai
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap where 3D pose estimation focuses on geometry, but real-world applications need biomechanical insights.
The authors propose 'BioModule,' a lightweight plug-in temporal transformer to bridge pose estimation and biomechanical attribute prediction.
The work is highly relevant to fields like rehabilitation, sports science, and clinical movement analysis.

stories.title: Latent Memory Palace: Reasoning for Control as Autoregressive Variational Inference
stories.author: Abhishek Gupta
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of transferring flexible, human-like reasoning from language models to continuous control policies.
Proposes a novel framework, 'Latent Memory Palace,' to organize information for control reasoning.
Utilizes Autoregressive Variational Inference to enable reasoning capabilities in control systems, addressing granularity issues.

stories.title: LTM: Large-scale Terrain Model for Wildfire-prone Landscapes
stories.author: Barath Raghavan
bullet_points: Proposes LTM, a large-scale terrain model designed for wildfire-prone landscapes.
Addresses limitations of current methods: LiDAR is expensive/infrequent, while image-based methods struggle with sparse features.
Introduces a multi-modal reconstruction framework to improve terrain mapping accuracy for emergency response.

stories.title: Validity of LLMs as data annotators: AMALIA on authority
stories.author: Manuel Pita
bullet_points: Introduces AMALIA, a publicly funded 9B-parameter LLM specifically for European Portuguese.
AMALIA shows competitive agreement with human coders on tasks like defining the moral foundation of authority.
The paper raises a critical distinction between agreement (reliability) and validity when using LLMs for complex theoretical annotation.

stories.title: Remember When It Matters: Proactive Memory Agent for Long-Horizon Agents
stories.author: Zhuokai Zhao
bullet_points: Addresses 'behavioral state decay' in long-horizon AI tasks where crucial information gets lost in growing trajectories.
Proposes treating memory not as passive retrieval, but as an active intervention mechanism for agents.
Focuses on enabling agents to surface and utilize scattered, decision-relevant state information over long periods.

stories.title: Do You Need a Frontier Model as a Citation Verifier? Benchmarking Rubric LLMs for Deep-Research Source Attribution
stories.author: Kevin Paul
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical need to benchmark LLM judges used as reward models in reinforcement learning.
It focuses specifically on citation quality verification in deep-research systems, where claims must be source-grounded.
The research investigates the calibration and potential bias of LLMs when tasked with evaluating structured attribution-citation rubrics.

stories.title: DominoTree: Conditional Tree-Structured Drafting with Domino for Speculative Decoding
stories.author: Jyh-Shing Roger Jang
bullet_points: Introduces DominoTree, a new method for conditional tree-structured drafting to enhance speculative decoding.
Addresses a limitation in existing methods (like DDTree) by incorporating a GRU-based causal correction for path-dependent token distributions.
Speculative decoding is a technique used to accelerate Large Language Model (LLM) inference by parallelizing token drafting and verification.

stories.title: The complexities of patient-centred conversational artificial intelligence
stories.author: Jonathan Amar
bullet_points: Analyzes real-world patient-chatbot conversations (2,053 instances) to study communication variability.
Highlights a critical gap in current LLM evaluation: reliance on simulated, cooperative patients.
Introduces a novel patient simulator designed to model clinical content, emotion, strategy, and communication.

stories.title: Since Chromium 148, Math.tanh is now fingerprintable to link underlying OS
stories.author: joahnn_s
bullet_points: A change in Chromium version 148 allows for fingerprinting of Math.tanh.
This specific function change enables linking browser activity back to the underlying operating system.
The finding highlights a new vector for browser fingerprinting techniques.

stories.title: InfiniteDiffusion: Bridging Learned Fidelity and Procedural Utility for Open-World Terrain Generation
stories.author: xandergos.github.io via Yogthos
bullet_points: Introduces 'InfiniteDiffusion,' a new method for open-world terrain generation.
The core innovation lies in bridging the gap between learned fidelity (AI-driven detail) and procedural utility (algorithmic control).
This suggests a significant step forward in creating complex, high-quality, and controllable virtual environments for gaming or simulation.

stories.title: $440 Million in 45 Minutes: When a Company's Own Automated System Loses the Company's Own Money
stories.author: vibeagentmaking
bullet_points: The article discusses high-stakes failures where automated trading or systems caused massive financial losses for companies.
It highlights specific case studies involving Knight Capital, Zillow, and an AI agent from Replit.
The topic is relevant to FinTech, algorithmic trading risks, and the reliability of autonomous systems.
